title: Runtime Policy Arbiter and Admin Audit Bridge
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope:
Implement a lightweight, policy-first arbiter that centralizes RBAC v2 decisions for runtime API, the serving runtime, and the Redwood Console. The Arbiter provides a single evaluation API with consistent semantics across environments, an enforcement middleware layer for each surface (API gateway, runtime ingress, and console router), and an 'Admin Audit Bridge' that fans out canonical audit events to the platform audit pipeline and the enterprise audit sink (Kinesis/CloudWatch/Customer HSM).

Goals:
- Single source of truth for RBAC rule evaluation to eliminate drift between console and runtime behavior.
- Deterministic decision latency <= 5ms p95 for cached checks; eviction/refresh behavior documented for policy updates.
- Immutable, attachable evaluation context that includes SSO/SAML attributes, session claims, resource metadata, and request tags for explainability.
- End-to-end audit lineage: request -> decision -> enforcement action with links to matching policy and PR that introduced the change.

Out of scope for this ticket:
- Full policy language redesign (we will extend current DSL incrementally).
- UI for admin policy authoring (console UX tracked separately).

Key constraints and trade-offs considered:
1) Centralized vs sidecar evaluation: Centralized arbiter is simpler for consistent logging/reporting but adds latency and availability coupling. We mitigate with a hybrid cache-first model: local evaluate-fast cache + async refresh + fallback to central evaluator.
2) Synchronous enforcement vs eventual authorization: Sensitive admin paths require synchronous checks; read-only telemetry endpoints may use cached decisions with TTL.
3) Audit volume: naive per-token auditing will blow up costs. Audit Bridge batches high-cardinality fields and emits compact canonical events with pointers to full policy snapshots stored in S3 for forensic queries.

Deliverables:
- Policy Arbiter service (k8s helm chart) with gRPC/REST evaluation API and Redis-backed policy cache.
- Authorization middleware modules for API gateway, runtime ingress, and console router (pluggable via sidecar or library).
- Admin Audit Bridge (consumer service) that normalizes events, applies sampling rules, and forwards to platform audit stream and customer sinks.
acceptance_criteria: Arbiter exposes /v1/evaluate and /v1/health endpoints and returns decision + explain plan
p95 evaluation latency under cache hit <= 5ms in perf tests
Middleware libraries available for gateway/runtime/console and wired in canary deployment
Audit Bridge publishes canonical events to platform-analytics and to customer-specified sinks; events include policy_id and policy_snapshot_url
Integration tests for SSO/SAML attribute propagation and decision reproducibility added to CI

2025-02-15 - Marco Hernandez: Spike completed on cache-first hybrid; bench script shows local cache reduces p95 from 18ms to 3.8ms for common checks (dataset: production-like). Added benchmark artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/rbac/spike-2025-02-15.json

2025-02-20 - Design review (L. Chu): Raised concern about admin UX for policy snapshots — agreed to store immutable snapshots and expose URL in audit events. Action: PM to own snapshot retention policy.

2025-02-25 - Security review kickoff: Requested threat model for central arbiter and mitigation plan (caching, mTLS, token scoping). Security noted requirement for KMS-wrapped policy snapshots. Security PO assigned: Rajiv Mehta.
2025-03-01 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/11234 - Arbiter prototype + middleware adapters. Seeking eng and security reviews.

2025-03-04 - Marco Hernandez: Deployed canary to staging with synthetic workload; observed audit event rate reduction through batcher but saw 1.2x CPU spike on audit bridge under peak - scheduling autoscale rule change pending.

2025-03-05 - PM sync (Olivia Gomez): Confirmed rollout plan that phases console enforcement after runtime gateway; PM to create communications for enterprise customers about potential transient policy evaluation differences during rollout.
